claims.statement: In the displayed binary model, let r_t=sigmoid(F v_t+B r_(t-1)+c) be the deterministic recurrent state. Set visible bias a_t=a+A r_(t-1) and hidden bias d_t=d+D r_(t-1). With hidden-by-visible weights W, define p(v_t,h_t|r_(t-1)) proportional to exp(a_t^T v_t+d_t^T h_t+h_t^T W v_t), and marginalize binary h_t for the frame distribution. The visible-sequence probability is the product of these conditional frame distributions; the current frame updates r_t only after its probability has been evaluated from r_(t-1). Recurrent and RBM hidden widths may differ, and W is distinct from recurrent input weights F. Train using conditional RBM likelihood statistics, approximated in the paper by data-started finite contrastive divergence, and backpropagate bias-gradient signals through A, D and the recurrence. The reverse state signal includes A^T and D^T times next-frame bias gradients, plus B^T times the next recurrent preactivation gradient. Generation alternates conditional frame sampling with the deterministic state update.

entries.name: RNN-NADE
entries.definition: A neural sequence architecture in which a deterministic recurrent state supplies parameters of a NADE output distribution, combining temporal recurrence with normalized within-frame autoregressive conditionals.
entries.identity_notes: This is the RNN-NADE identified in the 2012 recurrent-output-estimator paper by substituting NADE for the conditional RBM. Temporal order between vector frames and variable order within a frame are separate. The recurrent state and NADE prefix activations are deterministic computations; there is no stochastic RBM hidden state to integrate out. It is distinct from unconditional NADE, order-agnostic NADE, RNN-RBM and a recurrent predictor with independent Bernoulli outputs. limitations: Exact normalized probabilities and gradients apply to this specified model with fully observed training sequences. They do not imply global optimization, calibration, equality to an RBM distribution or tractable inference for every pattern of missing frames or bits.

The within-frame ordering and temporal recurrence serve different purposes. Prefix sharing gives O(DH) NADE evaluation per frame for H hidden units, in addition to the recurrent-state and bias-projection costs; it does not remove sequential generation dependencies.

The original NADE paper prints an accumulator index discrepancy and initializes a multiplicatively accumulated probability to zero with an incorrect plus between Bernoulli factors in Algorithm 1. The displayed mechanism follows its normalized chain definition, Equations (9)–(11) and prefix-update rule, retaining the source qualification.

Output weights V may be learned separately from W as in the original NADE paper. Sharing prefix parameters across conditionals does not require tying input and output weights, and it does not make within-frame variables independent.

The RNN-RBM paper’s negative joint/bias signs concern its RBM formulas and are not a prescription for NADE conditionals. Backpropagation through the separate recurrence still requires dimensionally correct transposes. No author-code or empirical superiority claim is certified.

claims.statement: For the single-layer binary specialization, compute the past-dependent biases b_t=b+P r_(t-1) and c_t=c+Q r_(t-1). Fix an ordering of D bits within the current frame. At position i, compute z_(t,i)=sigmoid(c_t+W[:,<i] v_(t,<i)) and q_(t,i)=sigmoid(b_(t,i)+V[i,:] z_(t,i)). Multiply q_(t,i) raised to v_(t,i) times (1-q_(t,i)) raised to (1-v_(t,i)) over positions, then multiply frame probabilities over time. Reuse a prefix accumulator initialized to c_t, adding W[:,i] v_(t,i) after evaluating each conditional. After the frame is observed or generated, update the separate recurrent state using its own input and recurrent weights. Differentiate the exact sum of frame negative log probabilities through the NADE parameters, the bias projections and the recurrent history. The 2012 paper explicitly contrasts these exact model gradients with CD-based RNN-RBM gradients. Ancestral generation samples bits in the fixed within-frame order before updating the recurrent state.

entries.name: Conditional restricted Boltzmann machine
entries.definition: A conditional neural probability model that represents an output vector with an RBM whose biases or interactions are determined by a supplied conditioning vector.
entries.identity_notes: This is the general input-conditioned RBM family described by Mnih, Larochelle and Hinton, with their affine-bias binary formulation as the explicitly curated mechanism. The conditioning vector need not be temporal history. Autoregressive CRBM fixes it to earlier frames and RNN-RBM derives it from a recurrent state; these are narrower constructions, not aliases for the entire family. HashCRBM and CD-PercLoss are separate training or prediction constructions and do not define every conditional RBM. limitations: The model specifies p(v|u), not the input marginal p(u). Normalizing outputs for one conditioning vector does not supply a shared partition for every other input or a joint model over arbitrary inputs.

Factorial block conditionals do not make the output marginal factorial or its partition, joint mode and coordinate marginals generally tractable. Tiny output spaces or deliberately restricted support are special cases.

A small data-started CD update can reflect poor mixing near the observed output rather than accurate predictions from u alone. Finite CD is not generally the exact conditional likelihood gradient or the gradient of a single fixed objective.

Persistent samples from one conditioning input cannot simply be treated as equilibrium samples for another. The paper’s discussion of persistent-chain impracticality is scoped to its input-specific distributions and training setting; it is not a proof that every conditional persistent method is impossible.

The general family can condition biases or interactions, while the displayed mechanism holds W_vh fixed and changes biases affinely. Gaussian outputs, input-dependent interactions, retrieved-support HashCRBM and perceptron-style training need separate conventions. No historical-priority, universal prediction-quality or author-code claim is asserted.

claims.statement: Hold conditioning vector u fixed. In the paper’s binary affine-bias specialization, set a(u)=b_v+(W_uv)^T u and c(u)=b_h+(W_uh)^T u, with visible-by-hidden interaction matrix W_vh. Define E(v,h;u)=-v^T W_vh h-a(u)^T v-c(u)^T h. Marginalizing binary h gives F(v,u)=-a(u)^T v-sum_j log(1+exp(c_j(u)+(W_vh^T v)_j)). Normalize exp(-F(v,u)) over output configurations v to obtain p(v|u), with a partition depending on u. Hidden units given v,u and visible units given h,u have factorial logistic conditionals, but outputs after hidden marginalization can be dependent. Conditional likelihood gradients contrast data-posterior and model expectations at the same u. The paper discusses finite CD as an approximation and separate alternatives for restricted output support or prediction-based training. Prediction may seek the joint conditional mode or coordinate-wise marginal modes according to the loss; those are different decisions.

native_neighbors.identity_notes: This is Sutskever, Hinton and Taylor’s 2008 RTRBM, with a real-valued recurrent state and separate binary within-step RBM hidden variables. Replacing a sampled TRBM hidden state by a deterministic probability vector changes the generative model; exact inference in RTRBM is not exact inference in the original stochastic TRBM. The recurrent update and conditional RBM share weights in this architecture. The real-valued state must not be conflated with the binary hidden variables integrated out of each output RBM. limitations: Exact deterministic-state inference requires the visible sequence to be observed. Missing observations require marginalizing uncertainty in visible values and induced recurrent states; the exact-inference statement does not automatically extend to that problem.

claims.statement: For input x, a neural network outputs parameters defining p(t|x)=sum_i alpha_i(x) phi_i(t|x). In the report’s c-dimensional isotropic Gaussian construction, softmax outputs give nonnegative mixing weights summing to one, direct outputs give component means, and exponentiated outputs give positive standard deviations sigma_i, with covariance sigma_i squared times the identity. The mixture can have dependent target coordinates even though coordinates are independent within each isotropic component. Minimize the sum of negative log mixture densities over input/target pairs. With responsibilities r_i=alpha_i phi_i/p(t|x), the output-logit derivative of one negative log likelihood is alpha_i-r_i; the mean derivative is r_i(mu_i-t)/sigma_i squared and the log-scale derivative is r_i(c-||t-mu_i|| squared/sigma_i squared). Backpropagate these derivatives through the network. Mixture weights are conditional component priors before observing t; responsibilities condition on both x and t. The conditional mean is the weighted mean of component centers and need not be a mode or a plausible branch of a multivalued inverse mapping.
